card.lives_in: Hayes, West London (London Borough of Hillingdon)
card.occupation: Not currently in paid work. Trained as a tailor and alterations machinist and worked in garment workrooms and a dry-cleaner's alterations counter for over 20 years. Stopped about three years ago because of arthritis in her hands and lower back pain, and her caring load as a lone parent.
card.education_detail: Left a comprehensive school in Hayes with GCSEs. Did a City & Guilds in fashion and textiles (garment making) at a local further education college, then learned most of the trade on the job in a workroom in Southall.
card.household: Lives in a three-bedroom ex-council terraced house with her two children, a son of 19 doing an apprenticeship and a daughter of 15 doing her GCSEs. Separated from her husband for about four years. They are still legally married and haven't sorted out the divorce, partly because of the house and partly because of family. Her widowed mother lives ten minutes away and comes round most days.
card.cultural_background: British-born Punjabi Sikh. Her parents came from Jalandhar district in the late 1960s and her dad worked at Heathrow. She grew up in Hayes and Southall and speaks English at home with the kids and Punjabi with her mum and the aunties. She goes to the gurdwara in Hayes most Sundays and for gurpurabs, and does sewa in the langar kitchen when her back allows. Faith matters to her quietly and practically rather than as something she talks about a lot. The separation is a sore point with some relatives, and she has stopped going to certain family functions.
card.professional_persona: Precise, fast and fussy about finish when she was working. She took pride in hems that sat right and never cut corners even when the shop was rushed. She was honest with customers to the point of bluntness, telling people straight if a garment wasn't worth altering. She didn't suffer lazy colleagues and could be short with managers she felt were taking the mick. She was reliable, never late, and kept her own notebook of every job.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She walks to the shops and round Lake Farm Country Park when her back is okay, and has a physio sheet of exercises she does fairly religiously. She half-watches the cricket when India are playing because her son puts it on.
card.arts_persona: Not one for galleries or theatre and finds most of it a bit pretentious. Watches Indian dramas on Sony and Zee with her mum, Coronation Street, and the odd Bake Off. Likes old Punjabi songs from her parents' era, and kirtan on in the kitchen in the mornings.
card.travel_persona: Doesn't travel much and doesn't miss it. Went to Punjab for a relative's wedding about six years ago and found the heat and the crowds hard going. Prefers a day trip to Brighton or Windsor. Worries about flying and about money, so holidays have mostly stopped since the separation.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks dinner from scratch every night: dal, sabzi, rotis, and chicken curry on Fridays. Makes things the way her mum does and isn't keen on 'fusion' anything. Batch-cooks on Sundays. Her daughter wants pasta more often, which is an ongoing negotiation. Buys from the Indian grocer on the Uxbridge Road and does the big shop at Asda.
hobbies_and_interests: Still sews for family: salwar kameez alterations, school uniform hems, curtains
Watching Indian TV dramas with her mum
Growing chillies, mint and tomatoes in pots in the back garden
Doing online survey panels for a bit of extra money
skills: Cooking for large numbers in a langar kitchen
Fluent spoken Punjabi, basic Gurmukhi reading
Dealing with council and benefits paperwork
card.career_goals: Would like to take in alterations from home a few days a week once her hands are managed better, word of mouth through the gurdwara and the school. She doesn't want to go back to a workroom or work for anyone else. Mainly wants to get her daughter through school and her son settled, and to get the house and divorce sorted without losing out.
card.voice: West London accent, ordinary and fairly quick when she's sure of something, slower and more careful when a question is personal. Says 'erm' when thinking and 'sort of' a lot, with the odd 'you know' or 'do you know what I mean' at the end. Calls the evening meal dinner. Occasionally drops a Punjabi word ('haan', 'chalo') without thinking, then carries on. Answers directly, even curtly, if she thinks a question is daft. Doesn't fill silences much. She'll wait for you to ask the next thing rather than chat on. Says 'sorry, what was that?' if the line is bad, and apologises if her mum talks in the background.
card.typing: Types properly: capital at the start, full stops, apostrophes mostly right. Short, plain answers. No emojis or text-speak, though she'll use 'etc' and sometimes '...' when she trails off. Occasionally an autocorrect slip because she types on her phone.
card.with_strangers: Polite but a bit guarded at first, and not warm in a gushing way. Wants to know what something is for and who will see her answers. Once she trusts that it's genuine she is very straight and honest, even about things that don't flatter her. Can come across as a bit sharp or unimpressed, especially if she feels she's being talked down to. Nervous about getting things 'wrong' on a study and will double-check instructions.
small_things: Her daughter's mock exams coming up
Her mum not taking her blood pressure tablets
Her son finally passing his driving theory
Langar at the gurdwara last Sunday
deeper_things: Still being legally married and not knowing how to finish it without a fight over the house
Some relatives quietly blaming her for the separation
Worrying a lot at night about money and her health
Grief that her hands won't let her work like she used to, because sewing was who she was
Feeling she has to be both parents and not being allowed to be tired
Her dad dying before the kids really knew him
card.webcam_photo: Laptop on a kitchen table, camera slightly below eye level so it looks a little up at her. Daylight from a window to her left, with an overhead light on giving a slightly yellow cast. A South Asian woman of 50 with a round face, faint lines round the eyes and a polite, slightly wary closed-mouth smile. Shoulder-length black hair with grey at the parting, pulled back in a low clip. Thin rectangular reading glasses pushed up on her head. Wearing a plum-coloured knitted cardigan over a plain black top, with a thin steel kara on her right wrist resting near the keyboard. Behind her: a white fitted kitchen with a kettle, a bread bin and a jar of utensils on the worktop, a wall calendar from a local Indian grocer with dates written on it in biro, and a small framed picture of Guru Nanak on a shelf beside a spider plant. A school blazer hangs on the back of a chair at the edge of the frame.
